con-vīso , ĕre, v. a. (rare and mostly ante-class.),
I.to consider attentively, look at, examine thoroughly: “omnia loca oculis,” Lucr. 2, 357 : “penitus res occultas,” id. 1, 146 : omnes saucios, Att. ap. Non. p. 398, 4 (Trag. Rel. v. 598 Rib.).—Poet.: “omnia loca candida luce (sol et luna),” Lucr. 5, 779 ; so Cic. Arat. 352.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
